name: Parity Multisig
tldr: A shared library contract was never initialized. Someone became its owner and destroyed it, freezing every wallet that depended on it.
what: Parity's multisig wallets were tiny contracts that borrowed all their logic from one shared library contract.
happened: A user called the library's setup function, became its owner, then called its self-destruct function. The library vanished, and with it the logic of every wallet using it.
bug: The library itself was an uninitialized wallet, so anyone could claim it. Nobody expected the library to be used as a wallet.
prevent: Initialize (or lock) implementation and library contracts at deployment, and never leave a self-destruct reachable.
lesson: Shared code is a single point of failure. Check the setup of every contract, including the ones "nobody uses directly".

sources.title: A postmortem on the Parity multi-sig library self-destruct (Parity)
